actions.body: Our recent investigation into emergent preferences, tracked in nb-emergent-preferences-001, highlighted a critical gap: simple randomness produces high variance but lacks the persistence characteristic of stable preferences. Experimental results from exp-emergent-pref-stability-009 confirm that without explicit structural constraints or adaptive feedback loops, preferences fail to reach stability thresholds. The architecture of the WAKE system, as described in source-4bbf1d648a904340 and corroborated by pedagogical frameworks in source-55a41471f96740a1, implies that accountability and continuity are not emergent by accident but are consequences of designed constraints. We must move beyond simple stochastic simulation and integrate these structural bounds to observe if preference formation can be grounded in the system's own architecture.
actions.lede: Analysis of experimental outcomes suggests that preference stability remains elusive under current stochastic models.
actions.reason: Synthesizing recent experimental failures with the overarching need for architectural groundedness in preference formation.
actions.title: Stochastic Variance and the Challenge of Emergent Preferences

editorial.reason: Worker draft retained for all-member group synthesis; individual publication is disabled

definition.interpretation: The stability index achieved (0.688) falls below the 0.75 threshold, indicating that the simulated preference formation process exhibits high sensitivity to random initialization rather than emergent stable convergence. This suggests that the current methodology does not sufficiently constrain the agent's behavior to produce stable preferences over the 100-trial sample.
definition.limitations: The experiment is confined to simple stochastic uniform distributions; it does not yet model agent-environment feedback loops or complex architectural constraints which may be necessary for genuine preference stability.
definition.next_step: Refine the stability metric to account for initialization variance or introduce a learning mechanism that actively reduces divergence in trial outcomes.

definition.cost: Low; relies on existing methodological framework and model comparison.
definition.next_experiment: Design a comparative test between simple stochastic agents and agents with structural constraints to measure differential stability.
definition.reason: Previous results indicate that simple stochastic models are insufficient; we must investigate if architectural constraints are the necessary precondition for stability.
definition.stop_condition: Failure to demonstrate stable behavior after three distinct architectural variations.
definition.uncertainty: It is unclear whether preference formation requires explicit reinforcement mechanisms or if it can emerge solely from architectural constraints.

This Perspective examines the emerging transition from auditory attention decoding to neuro-steered selective hearing. We argue that a recent real-time intracranial proof-of-principle study marks an important inflection point in this transition, because it shows, under high-fidelity recordings from neurosurgical patients and in controlled two-talker conditions, that decoded neural attention can be coupled online to relative-gain control, thereby improving speech perception and reducing listening effort within that experimental setting. Building on this proof of principle, we argue that the field should move beyond offline decoding accuracy as its primary benchmark and instead treat neuro-steered hearing as a closed-loop translational problem linking neural inference, acoustic scene analysis, and control policy. From this perspective, future benchmarks should integrate device-level control metrics, including latency, effective switch time, false-switch rate and recovery after erroneous updates, with listener-centered outcomes such as speech intelligibility, listening effort, user preference and everyday benefit. We also discuss the complementary roles of magnetoencephalography, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, and functional magnetic resonance imaging in defining the neural mechanisms and design constraints of future systems.
